units.text: Background and Aims: Smoking has been a major problem among college student in Indonesia. Smoking can lead to several respiratory disease and declined pulmonary function. This study was done to determine the association between smoking behavior and characteristic of respiratory symptoms and lung function among college students. Methods: This study used a cross-sectional study method with questionnaire and measurement kit as it's instrument. Questionnaire consist of ATS (American Thoracic Society) questionnaire for respiratory symptoms and Brinkman index for smoking behaviour one. EasyOne ® Air Spirometer is used to measured lung function in this study. Subjects were recruited from 116 college students who were active smokers. The data obtained were analysed with non-parametric Mann-Whitney test, independent t-test, and bivariate spearmen test. Results: The study showed majority of 116 subjects are mild (96.6%) and only 3.4% moderate-severe Brinkman index. Respiratory complained found in 74.1% subjects which were cough (32.8%), sputum (44%), and shortness of breath (12.1%). We found 15.5% lung function impairment with 8.6% of subjects had obstructive and 6.9% had restrictive. There was no statistically significant association between smoking habits among smoke student with respiratory symptoms (p 0.148) and pulmonary function (p 0.231). Conclusion: This study showed college students have respiratory symptoms and lung function impairment but found no association with smoking habits. However, smoking behavior among college students still need more attention as a public health problem. Keywords: Brinkman index, college students, pulmonary function, respiratory symptoms. Background and Aims: We have previously shown that the regular use of soy products reduces the susceptibility of a healthy person to acute respiratory infections 1 . We aimed to study the dynamics of quality of life (QoL) during the COVID-19 pandemic when soy-pumpkin products are included in the diet. Methods: 34 healthy people aged 18 to 53 years of both sexes were interviewed. The main group (n=17), in addition to the usual diet for 10 weeks, received originally prepared soy-pumpkin products (drink and dessert), the control group (n=17) was on a regular diet. Overall QoL was studied using the MOS SF-36 questionnaire. Results: Comparative analysis showed an increase in QoL in the main group in the domains Physical Functioning (from 92.3AE1.7 to 95.6AE1.6 points; p=0.0112), General Health (from 56.9AE3.2 to 66,5AE2.4; p=0.0147), Vitality (from 52.3AE2.6 to 72.3AE2.9; p=0.001), Mental Health (from 64.9AE2, 7 to 76.5AE3.2; p=0.0007). At the beginning of the study, the Social Functioning (SF) in the main and control groups was low (44.3AE2.4 vs. 47.1AE1.7; p=0.3239). By the end of the study, in the main group it remained at the same level, and in the control group, a decrease in SF was observed (from 47.1AE1, 7 to 38.5AE4.0; p=0.0355), probably due to the introduction of restrictive quarantine requirements during a pandemic. Conclusion: A regular use of soy-pumpkin products for 10 weeks improves the physical and psychological components of QoL, prevents a decrease in self-esteem of social functioning in conditions of self-isolation.
